surface: Cells whose values arrive later: the pending state, a value that resolves on the cell the user is on, and a request that fails there.

steps.note: Two requests are out for the Name column, rows 1 and 2. The cell keeps its old value, `Old A`, and carries the visually hidden text `Loading...`, because no common reader says `aria-busy` on a cell. VoiceOver said nothing on this first key in some runs, with WebKit and with Chromium, as on the first key of other scenarios.

The server answers the request for the cell the user is on with `New A`. The plugin announces no resolved value. Finding: NVDA and VoiceOver with Chromium say nothing, so a reader is not told that the value it read as loading has arrived; with Firefox and WebKit they read the cell again.
The next row's cell is still pending. Finding: VoiceOver with WebKit runs the visually hidden text into the value (`Old BLoading...`), so neither reads on its own.
The request for the cell the user is on fails, and the plugin announces its message (polite).
The first cell holds the value that arrived.

The failed cell keeps its old value and carries the error message as visually hidden text, read with the cell. Finding: VoiceOver with WebKit runs the message into the value (`Old BPrice service unavailable`), as with the pending text.
